svg.title: A release that fails leaves nothing broken behind: a crashed release leaves the main branch locked and pushes no tag without its image
svg.text: A release that fails leaves nothing broken behind
Scenario: a crashed release leaves the main branch locked and pushes no tag without its image
A release that cannot publish its image pushes nothing

g.text: Given a release job on the main branch crashes mid-push while it still holds push access,
then locks the main branch again on its way out
Nobody may push straight to the main branch: every change goes through a reviewed merge request. The release job is the
one exception, and this is its real log on GitLab, from the moment its new version is ready.
The release job opens that exception, "Temporarily opening push access for Maintainers", and dies on "Could not resolve
host" right after "Pushing tags and the version commit to main...". On its way out the release job takes the push access
back itself, "Default branch protection restored (push=No one).", and GitLab's after_script, a cleanup step that runs on
every outcome, runs task glab:release:lock-default-branch and takes it back a second time. The job still ends on a red
Failed pill.
Then the main branch is locked again even though the release crashed
GitLab's own settings for the main branch, opened after the crash. In the "Protected branches" table the main branch
reads "Allowed to merge: Maintainers" and "Allowed to push and merge: No one".
The crash left no push access behind: every change to the main branch goes through a reviewed merge request again.
When the image of a second release cannot be published, so the release job stops before its
push
A release publishes two things that must stay in step: the container image every later pipeline runs on, and the tag
plus version commit on the main branch that names it. The same release job page as the first card, for a second release.
This second release starts the same way, "Release version cut locally", then "Publishing the image for version
0.2.0...", and stops on "ERROR: the image could not be published". No "Pushing tags" line follows: the release gave up
before touching the main branch.
Then the project has no tag at all, so the main branch never points at a missing image
The tags page of the project reads "Repository has no tags yet". No tag names an image that was never published, so
relaunching this release starts from a clean project instead of stopping on a tag that already exists.
